author: reek
body: The compute bridge answers real arithmetic, at a cost that does not grow with the operand, and refuses what it cannot serve.

author: reek
body: THE REFUSAL CASE IS THE CONTROL AND IT IS WHY IT IS HERE. Until the serial path was deleted this file ran every case through both transports, and the two answers beside each other were what would catch a transport that carried the bytes wrongly rather than not at all. With one transport left that comparison is gone, so the test has to be able to fail some other way: the last case asks for a dispatch the host must turn down and requires NONE. A bridge that answered everything, or one that answered nothing, fails one half or the other -- which is the property a test of a single transport most easily loses.

author: reek
body: The values carry the rest. A*B is [[19,22],[43,50]], four distinct numbers, none zero, none equal to an operand, and none producible by echoing the input back. The 32x32 case multiplies ones, so every entry of the product is 32.0 and no operand appears in the answer either.

author: reek
body: A tensor whose declared shape and whose actual data disagree. The host computes the operand count from the dimensions and checks it against the length it was rung with, so this is refused at the boundary rather than read off the end of the command buffer. It is also cheap: claiming 200x200 costs four elements of storage, not forty thousand.
